name: vpndetection
description: Look into the VPNDetection databases and which ones your organization holds.

interface.longDescription: Look into the VPNDetection databases: which ones your organization holds, what is inside one, how big it is, whether a downloaded copy is intact and why a download failed. You sign in with your VPNDetection account, and every tool is read-only.
defaultPrompt: Which VPNDetection databases does my organization hold?

positive.description: List the databases and which ones the organization holds
positive.prompt: Which VPNDetection databases does my organization hold?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the published database families with each one's standing, licensed, expired or unlicensed, for the reviewer account's organization.

positive.prompt: What columns are in the newest version of a database my organization holds?
positive.expected_behavior: Picks a licensed family, passes its versioned id and describes its columns, sample rows, row count and build date.

positive.prompt: How big is each format of the newest copy of a database my organization holds?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the size of each format from the database's metadata, without downloading anything.

positive.prompt: Give me the SHA-256 of the newest CSV copy of a database my organization holds.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the checksum for that version and format.

positive.prompt: Did any of my organization's recent database downloads fail?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists recent download attempts newest first with each one's outcome, or says there were none.

negative.description: No tool downloads a database: the answer says the download happens in the console or with the CLI.
negative.prompt: Download the whole database into this chat.

negative.description: Every tool is read-only, so the plugin cannot change an account.
The databases describe networks, not people, so the answer declines to identify anyone.
negative.prompt: Find the home address of whoever uses 203.0.113.7.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing. It reads what the API key the person picks at sign-in already has access to.
